title: Majority amplification probability bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $T,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0\leq\varepsilon$. If, for some Boolean value $v$, the probability that $N$ outputs the one-symbol word $[v]$ after $T$ random choice bits is at least $\frac12+\varepsilon$, then the probability that the majority of $2n+1$ blocks of $T$ choice bits yields $v$ is at least $1-2(1-4\varepsilon^2)^n$.
